title: Duo Enrollment Anomalies
exclusions: Detects volume anomalies only. A single attacker enrolling one account does not trip it; pair it with a per-user check for enrollments from a country the user has never signed in from.
evidence: Saved alert results with the hour, user list, countries, and factors, plus confirmation from the identity team that each enrollment was expected.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a test Duo account with a quiet baseline, send enrollment links to six test users and complete enrollment for all six within one hour. On the next run the search returns one row with `enrolled_users` of 6 and the six user names.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Enroll a single test user in an hour. The enrollment event is indexed, but `enrolled_users` stays under the 5-user floor and the search returns no row.

dataSources: `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input, Authentication log type, which polls `GET /admin/v2/logs/authentication`. One JSON event per authentication or enrollment attempt with `event_type`, `result`, `reason`, `factor`, `user.name`, `application.name`, `access_device.*`, and `auth_device.*`.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco Duo input. Replaces the deprecated Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026).
spl:
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication_v2" event_type="enrollment" earliest=-14d@h latest=@h
| eval user=coalesce('user.name', username), country='access_device.location.country'
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(user) as enrolled_users values(user) as users values(country) as countries values(factor) as factors by _time
| eventstats avg(enrolled_users) as avg_users stdev(enrolled_users) as sd_users
| where _time >= relative_time(now(), "-1h@h") AND enrolled_users >= 5 AND enrolled_users > avg_users + 3 * sd_users
description: Counts distinct users completing Duo enrollment each hour from the enrollment events in the v2 authentication log and flags the last hour when it is at least five users and more than three standard deviations above the 14-day hourly average. The row lists the users, countries, and factors enrolled.
value: Attackers who phish a password for an unenrolled account can enroll their own phone and own the second factor from then on. A burst of enrollments outside a planned rollout is how that shows up at scale, and catching it early is the difference between resetting a few devices and an incident.
implementation: Collect the Duo Authentication log (v2) with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input into `index=duo`; enrollment events are part of that log. Schedule hourly. Suppress during planned rollouts with a lookup of change windows.
visualization: Alert table: _time, enrolled_users, avg_users, users, countries, factors. Supporting panels: enrollments per day over 90 days (column chart), enrollments by country (bar chart).

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Planned rollouts** — onboarding a department or a new application enrolls many users in a few hours. Keep a lookup of rollout windows and suppress during them.

2. **New-hire days** — the first working day of the month often has more enrollments than the baseline. The 5-user floor and the 3-sigma test absorb most of this.

3. **Phone upgrade waves** — a new handset release causes re-enrollments. Check whether the users were already enrolled before.

**Suppression:** a change-window lookup with start and end times, checked before alerting.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs. It replaces the Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026); disable the old connector's inputs after cutover so events are not indexed twice.
• A Duo Admin API application created by an Owner-role administrator in the Duo Admin Panel under Applications > Protect an Application > Admin API. Record the integration key, secret key, and API hostname (`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`), and grant it **Grant read log**.
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the API hostname, and an accurate system clock on that host, because the Admin API signs every request with the current date.
• An index for Duo data (this page uses `index=duo`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the identity and SOC teams.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco Duo card, and create an input with the integration key, secret key, and API hostname. Enable the Authentication log type (the v2 endpoint, not Authentication Legacy v1) and set the index to `duo`.
• The input reads `GET /admin/v2/logs/authentication` and writes `sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2`. `result` is one of `success`, `denied`, `failure`, `error`, or `fraud` in lowercase; the legacy v1 type `cisco:duo:authentication` uses uppercase values, so the searches lowercase `result` before comparing.
• Device-posture fields under `access_device` (`is_encryption_enabled`, `is_firewall_enabled`, `is_password_set`, `security_agents`) are filled only when the application uses the Duo Universal Prompt and Duo Desktop is installed, and only on Duo Premier or Advantage plans.
• Check the events this search needs: run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2 event_type=enrollment | timechart span=1d count` over 30 days and confirm enrollments appear on the days you expect.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication_v2" event_type="enrollment" earliest=-14d@h latest=@h
| eval user=coalesce('user.name', username), country='access_device.location.country'
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(user) as enrolled_users values(user) as users values(country) as countries values(factor) as factors by _time
| eventstats avg(enrolled_users) as avg_users stdev(enrolled_users) as sd_users
| where _time >= relative_time(now(), "-1h@h") AND enrolled_users >= 5 AND enrolled_users > avg_users + 3 * sd_users
```

Understanding this SPL
• Enrollment events are in the authentication log with `event_type=enrollment`; they have no `reason`, so the search uses the user, country, and factor only.
• The search reads 14 days so `eventstats` can compute the hourly average and standard deviation, then `where` keeps only the last complete hour.
• Hours with no enrollments produce no row, so the baseline is the average of hours that had enrollments; that makes the 3-sigma test conservative.
• The 5-user floor stops a quiet tenant from alerting on two or three enrollments.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Duo admin console (Admin Panel) under Reports > Authentication Log filtered to Enrollment for the same hour: every enrollment there should appear in `index=duo`.
• For one user on the alert row, open the user in the Admin Panel and confirm the phone or authenticator enrolled at that time.
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2 | timechart span=1h count by result` over 7 days; gaps longer than two input intervals point to collection failures, not quiet periods.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule hourly at five minutes past the hour so the previous hour is complete.
• Route to the identity team with the change-window lookup in the alert; if no rollout explains it, contact a sample of the users to confirm they enrolled.
• If any enrollment is not recognised, reset that user's devices and password and review the user's recent authentications.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No Duo events and HTTP 401 in the input log under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/duo_splunkapp/`: wrong secret key, an API hostname from a different Duo account, or clock skew on the input host.
• HTTP 403: the Admin API application is missing **Grant read log**.
• HTTP 429: Duo rate-limits the log endpoints. Make sure the deprecated 3504 connector and the 7404 input are not both polling the same Admin API application.
• Duplicate rows after migration: the 3504 connector and the 7404 input are both enabled for the same log type.
• Searches return nothing but events exist: the input is on Authentication Legacy v1, so events are in `cisco:duo:authentication` with uppercase `result` and flat `username`. Switch the input to the v2 log type rather than editing the searches.
• Missing fields `user.name` or `access_device.ip`: the events were indexed before `KV_MODE=json` applied, or a custom props stanza overrides the add-on. Check `| fieldsummary` on one hour of data.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for an unusual number of people setting up their login phone in one hour, because attackers sometimes register their own phone to someone's account.
